Tomato___Bacterial_spot: Bacterial spot on tomato, caused by Xanthomonas, creates small water-soaked lesions that can merge into large necrotic patches.
Tomato___Early_blight: Early blight is marked by dark concentric rings on tomato leaves and stems, often starting on older foliage.
Tomato___Late_blight: Tomato late blight causes water-soaked lesions that quickly expand, often with white mold on leaf undersides in moist conditions.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot: Septoria leaf spot produces numerous small, circular spots with dark margins, typically starting on lower leaves.
Tomato___Spider_mites_Two_spotted_spider: Two-spotted spider mites feed on tomato leaf cells, causing stippling, bronzing, and eventual leaf drop under hot, dry conditions.
Tomato___Target_Spot: Target spot leads to brown necrotic lesions with concentric rings, resembling a target, often expanding during humid weather.
Tomato___Tomato_YellowLeaf__Curl_Virus: TYLCV is spread by whiteflies and causes upward leaf curling, stunted growth, and severe yield loss in tomato plants.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus: TMV causes mottling, mosaic patterns, and distorted growth in tomatoes — it is highly stable and spreads via mechanical contact.
Potato___healthy: Healthy potato plants produce lush green foliage and form uniform tubers when grown in well-drained, nutrient-rich soil.
